title: Uniform-routing and frozen-skill drops do not identify a new co-evolution interaction
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that Skill Self-Play's Uniform routing and Frozen skills ablation drops identify a new nonseparable skill-router or skill-curriculum co-evolution mechanism merely because each ablation reduces final accuracy.

fresh_phenomenon_closure.closure_scope: the reported Uniform routing and Frozen skills accuracy drops only

counter_explanation.statement: The two ablations remove different ordinary resources. Uniform routing weakens query/task-conditioned curriculum allocation while retaining the evolving skill mechanism; Frozen skills holds the available skill library fixed while retaining skill-guided generation. Large marginal drops from weakening allocation and from weakening the available expert/curriculum set are both predicted by standard expert-set quality plus gating/allocation decompositions and do not identify an interaction term. The same paper's policy co-evolution ablation is consistent with this interpretation: Frozen proposer causes a 2.1-point drop, Frozen feedback solver a 3.0-point drop, and Frozen both a 3.2-point drop, which is not evidence of a super-additive co-evolution cliff and is compatible with overlapping/complementary resources.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: With task information and training budget fixed, final utility can fall either because the evolving skill/curriculum set contains worse or less diverse training opportunities, or because the allocation policy selects those opportunities poorly. Both marginal effects can be substantial without a new nonseparable self-evolution primitive. A genuine interaction requires a matched factorial contrast that cannot be represented by skill-set quality plus allocation/selector regret under the same information.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Skill-set quality and curriculum/routing quality are separable resources until a matched same-information factorial demonstrates a residual interaction; separate component ablations do not establish co-evolutionary nonseparability.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Search only for a preregistered matched 2x2 design that independently varies library evolution and routing/allocation while holding backbone, task distribution, candidate skill contents where required, proposer/solver information, training tokens, and evaluation budget comparable. Require a repeatable held-out non-additive interaction beyond same-information expert-set quality, contextual routing, mixture-of-experts gating, curriculum allocation, and selector-regret baselines. Do not reopen from another pair of large marginal ablation drops.
counter_explanation.scope: Skill Self-Play arXiv:2607.22529, especially Table 3 Static skill orchestration and Table 4 Co-evolutionary updates.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: Uniform routing and Frozen skills are symmetric interventions on one variable: false; one changes allocation and the other changes the available/evolving skill set.
The two Table 3 drops estimate a factorial interaction: false; they are separate one-factor ablations.

The policy co-evolution ablation demonstrates super-additivity: the reported Frozen both drop is 3.2 points versus 2.1 and 3.0 points for the individual policy freezes, which does not establish a super-additive interaction.
The closure implies dynamic skills or routing are unnecessary: false; both can be useful while the standalone interaction claim remains unidentified.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only with a preregistered matched factorial comparison that independently varies skill/library evolution and routing/allocation under comparable task distribution, backbone, candidate-set information, training/evaluation budget, and supervision, and shows a repeatable non-additive held-out interaction that same-information expert-set quality, contextual routing, mixture-of-experts gating, curriculum allocation, and selector-regret models cannot express.

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: Skill Self-Play provides evidence that both dynamic skill evolution and non-uniform curriculum allocation contribute to performance. The cited pair of marginal ablations does not by itself establish a new nonseparable co-evolution mechanism.
